WILDKIN — VERSION 1 CANON & ART PRODUCTION CHECKLIST
Claude Code / SOL shared handoff • reconstructed from October 1–2, 2026 planning conversations • 12 October 2026
STATUS: COMPLETE NAMED ROSTER RECOVERED. The original October 2, 2026 First Bond list has now been reconstructed as 180 numbered names (Appendix A). This verifies names and category allocations, not yet card rules, per-card art briefs, or the detailed mechanics of the new set.
# 1. Division of work
Claude Code owns the game mechanics, cards, data identifiers, auto-import, validation, builds and tests. SOL owns the images, cut-sheets and artwork metadata. Both consume one committed canonical manifest. SOL pushes to a dedicated art branch/path; automatic CI validates, ingests and publishes on successful merge. A manual second Claude Code pass is not required for routine uploads.

# 7. Standard output specifications
- All cut-sheets: 3 columns × 3 rows; thin clean gutters; 10% empty margin around each subject, never crop appendages.
- Mascots: 9 clearly different poses for a character/species as required, with stable proportions and markings.
- Ordinary creatures: typically 3 core poses per species, arranged as 3 creatures × 3 poses on one 3×3 sheet where specified.
- Creature cutout background: flat chroma-green, chroma-magenta for green creatures; neutral front lighting, no text or frames.
- Consistent dimensional stylized 3D rendering, soft light, similar scale and quality across all sheets.
- Biome backgrounds: 3D-styled and compositionally suited for card scenes; dusk and iron backgrounds were explicitly flagged as missing.
- Premium art: real alternate illustration/composition, not recolored or resized base cutouts.
- Cutout subjects, biome backgrounds, evolutions, rarity effects and complete card renderings must remain separate layers; Claude Code builds card frames and text.
- Keep original 3×3 PNGs, extracted cutouts, manifest IDs, generation provenance and review states.
# 8. Energy affinities and set ecology
Nine established affinities: Verdant, Tide, Stone, Iron, Ember, Storm, Astral, Dusk, Wonder. These replace/override any old provisional type naming only after explicit mapping and rules compatibility checks. The existing code currently uses another nine-type vocabulary; build a deliberate migration rather than merely relabeling UI.
Long-term species plan: approximately 40 mascots and 100–110 ordinary/lesser roots, with evolution forms expanding the library to roughly 245 forms. Library estimate: 40 × 9 mascot poses + 100 × 3 ordinary poses = 660 cutouts. This is the long-term library, not a requirement for all 180 Set 001 cards.
# 9. Repository implementation and ownership rules
- Existing repository: oddlyprompt/CollectorGames; existing Wildkin app: docs/tcg. Preserve its gameplay, economy, saves and tests.
- Existing ingestion utility: tools/ingest.py. Existing build: tools/build.py --publish.
- Maintain immutable IDs for species, cards, images and set releases. Treat existing procedural art and creature names as provisional unless confirmed.
- Claude Code owns canonical data, card renderer, pack logic, mapping/ingestion, automated tests, versioned save strategy.
- SOL owns artwork only and commits generated files plus metadata to art-specific paths/branch.
- Use automated GitHub CI to lint filename schema, image size, aspect ratios, key colors, subject boundaries, completeness, and ID consistency; require approval before promotion to production assets.
- No two agents should independently edit the same canonical manifest. SOL must never silently alter card identities or new set allocations.
- Automated build after merged art commits; only invoke Claude Code again for structural change, test failures, or major art-mapping exceptions.

# 11. Canon gaps requiring source reconciliation
All 180 card names have now been recovered and numbered in Appendix A. Remaining reconciliation concerns exact card mechanics, evolution and rarity implementation, detailed art briefs and sheet-cell mapping, and the final reconciliation of those identities against the existing provisional code. No invented substitutes should be used.
The source-code test set and its older creature roster were explicitly described by the owner as a framework to be repopulated. Never mistake existing placeholder content for canon merely because it appears in current JavaScript.

APPENDIX B — AUTOMATION GATES
- Claude Code must ingest Appendix A as a complete locked 180-record manifest, with category and card number stored explicitly. Do not generate additional card names to fill perceived gaps.
- SOL must read the same versioned manifest and commit generated image sheets and associated asset metadata to the agreed art directory, without editing canonical card records.
- Existing 43-sheet queue remains a production plan; confirm cell assignments and source references before generating each sheet. Four SIR works are separate individual illustrations.
- GitHub automation validates image dimensions, expected slots, chroma backgrounds for cutouts, filenames and mappings; successful validated commits trigger the ingest/build flow.
- Card rules, attack text, exact art prompts and detailed per-card rarity mechanics not established in the historical named roster require explicit design reconciliation rather than fabricated canon.
